text:
Priya: quick pulse 10min7: we need to finalize the post-launch iteration plan. main split: urgent customer fixes vs. polish/enhancements. who9s on for a fast decision?
Ben: here. can we define a triage ladder so we don't debate each ticket?
Carlos: propose ladder = impact x scope x reproducibility. if impact >= enterprise-critical OR reproducible by CI test -> fast lane. otherwise schedule to enhancement backlog.
Tara: add a separate rule for perf regressions: any change that bumps p99 > 15% or increases CPU by >25% -> escalate.
Aisha: customers expect quick followups. suggest we call the fast lane the "48/5" policy: 48h ack, 5 business day plan. delivery target = next 2 sprints unless infra/security.
Priya: +1 to 48/5. also let's reserve a rotating triage slot (1 engineer per sprint) to pick up the fast lane items.
Ben: rollout guardrails? we should require a canary staircase: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with checks at each step. ops-bot can post checks.
ops-bot: canary pipeline created: redwood/canary-staircase v1. smoke jobs will run at each step. :robot_face:
Carlos: checklist for each release (I'll add to the runbook):
```
- unit/integration smoke
- canary smoke (latency & error rate)
- small customer pilot (if customer-impact tag)
- quality eval (subset compare to baseline)
- rollback window & owner
```
Tara: who is rollback owner? ops oncall + release engineer? add explicit names per release.
Priya: owners template: quality = Carlos, customer comms = Ben, release = Tara, monitoring = ops-oncall. we will fill person in card.
Aisha: backlog grooming tweak: tag items with "customer-pilot", "dev-days" (estimate), and "acceptance-criteria". run a 20m pre-groom to sort top 10 by customer-impact/dev-days ratio.
Ben: agree. also require acceptance criteria that includes both functional test and a basic telemetry assertion (e.g., no >5% increase in error rate).
Carlos: about temporary model tweaks (quantization, smaller model) -- add a quality regression check: compare hallucination rate on eval set and reject if > baseline + 2%.
Priya: let's document escalation thresholds for P1/P2 counts. we shouldn't expand scope if >1 outstanding P1 or if any active customer-blocking regression.
Aisha: pilot cohort volunteers: Acme, Nuvem, BrightData. we'll flip canary flag and collect feedback in a shared doc.
Tara: timeline: by EOD owners add dev-day estimates and acceptance criteria to sprint cards. we confirm at 11am huddle.
Ben: pulling estimates now.
Carlos: updating runbook with canary staircase and checklist.
ops-bot: reminder set: 11:00 Post-launch iteration confirm.
Priya: thanks everyone. short and practical. :thumbsup:
